title: Incident heatmap + ops sync prep (2026-05-15)
content:
Purpose:
Quick prep notes for the weekly SRE ops sync. Focus: incident heatmap review, paging trend validation, short/medium term mitigations to reduce noise and protect SLOs. Scratchpad — will tidy for meeting notes afterwards.

TL;DR summary (to open the sync):
- Error budget: hosted-api request success SLO 99.95% monthly. Current 7-day burn ~6.8% (extrapolated monthly ~28% if current trend continues).
- Pager volume: 30-day page count = 52 pages, +24% WoW. Spike concentrated in two clusters: model-serving (GPU OOM / reclaim flaps) and autoscaler flapping during bursts.
- Top recent incidents (for quick review): INC-2026-045 (GPU OOM cascade 2026-05-06), INC-2026-049 (autoscaler race 2026-05-10), INC-2026-052 (auth token expiry edge-case 2026-05-13).

Key metrics to surface (bring dashboards):
- Monthly SLO consumption (hosted-api success) — last 30/7/1 day lines
- P95 latency for generate endpoints (tokens/sec) — baseline vs last 7 days
- Pager heatmap: origin service + hour-of-day clustering (link above)
- Oncall escalations vs acknowledged pages ratio (noise metric)

Observations / hypotheses (unstructured notes):
- GPU OOM cascade seems correlated with a new model variant rollout on 2026-05-05 (SERVE-1122). KV cache miss patterns look different for that variant — larger memory working set. Hypothesis: kernel memory pressure + aggressive autoscaler response -> pod churn -> cascading requeues.
- Autoscaler flaps often when we get short bursts of concurrent long-context requests (dedicated customers hitting high seq lengths). We have conservative pod stabilization window; maybe too short.
- Auth token expiry pages look like downstream client clock skew + our cache TTL mismatch — low-severity but noisy.

Immediate mitigations (short term, 0-72h):
- Roll back model variant for the most affected pool (owner: Maya) — temp mitigation until memory profile validated (owner: Maya Rodriguez, ticket SERVE-1122-RB).
- Throttle long-context bursting via rate-limit circuit on Dedicated pools for new customers: quick rule patch (owner: Noah, SRE-456). Target: reduce autoscaler triggers by 50% in next 24h.
- Adjust autoscaler stabilization window from 30s -> 90s for affected nodepools (owner: Liam, INFRA-789). Monitor for increased latency.
- Suppress low-value auth token pages: add 1st-line filter rule to treat specific token-expiry tracer as warning-not-page (owner: Aisha).

Medium-term remediation (2–6 weeks):
- Memory profiling for model variant: run reproducer load + heap sampling, build smaller kv-blocking patch or recommend quantized variant (owner: Applied ML + Serving Runtime). Jira: SERVE-1150.
- Autoscaler policy change: add smarter burst-detection (recent-burst smoothing) and per-customer stabilization knobs. RFC in 2 weeks. (owner: infra-psf).
- Add prefix/KV caching metrics to per-route dashboards so we can see cache hit ratio correlated with memory pressure (owner: Observability).

Agenda (30 minutes total):
- 0–5m: quick numbers & heatmap snapshot (I'll share dashboard)
- 5–12m: incident recaps (INC-2026-045, 049, 052) — 3 min each + 1 min clarifying questions
- 12–18m: short-term mitigations and who does what (confirm rollbacks/suppressions)
- 18–25m: medium-term plan signoffs (autoscaler policy / profiling timeline)
- 25–30m: open blockers / ask for decisions from PLs / escalation path check

Questions I want to ask during sync (notes to self):
- To Product: can we gate the model rollout for customers on Dedicated vs Shared? If not, how do we signal customers about memory profile changes?
- To Applied ML: is there a cheaper quantized candidate that holds perf for the top-10 queries?
- To Platform: can we provision a short-lived warm standby pool (fractional GPUs) to absorb redeploy spikes? Cost estimate?

Suggested speaking points (for lead):
- "We have actionable short-term mitigations that should cut immediate noise by ~50%; we need two 24–72h operations to confirm (rollback + autoscaler tweak)."
- "If burns continue, we will temporarily gate new model rollouts to smaller cohorts while we validate memory profile."

Follow-ups / action items (capture after meeting):
- Maya: roll back problematic model variant and open postmortem stub (due 2026-05-16) -> SERVE-1122-RB
- Liam: implement autoscaler stabilization change in canary pool + monitor (due 2026-05-17) -> INFRA-789-1
- Noah: emergency rate-limit rule deployed to Dedicated pools (due 2026-05-16) -> SRE-456-2
- Aisha: push suppression rule for auth-token noise + update oncall doc (due 2026-05-16)
- Observability: add cache-hit metric to route dashboard (due 2026-05-28)
- Applied ML + Serving runtime: schedule memory profiling + run reproducer (due 2026-05-29) -> SERVE-1150

Quick notes on communication:
- Slack channel to use: #ops-incident-heatmap (create if missing). Post concise daily updates until burn rate below 10% weekly.
- PM/Customer comms: only if rollback affects SLAs or customer-facing behavior — draft email template if needed (ask PLs).

Scratch reminders (personal):
- Capture sample traces from 2026-05-06 OOMs and attach to SERVE-1122-RB.
- Run synthetic traffic profile that mimics 3x long-seq bursts to try and trigger autoscaler in staging.
- Revisit long-tail p99 latency alarm thresholds after autoscaler stabilization change (may need bump).

Unresolved / parking lot:
- Do we allow per-customer memory caps in Dedicated? Legal/contract implications? (ask contract ops)
- Long-term: is unified autoscaler for both hosted and dedicated causing cross-noise? Consider split.

-- end scratchpad --
